persona: MBA student running an in-person customer satisfaction intercept survey for a local cafe as part of a marketing capstone project
source_style: typed by hand into Excel each evening from paper survey forms filled out by customers in the cafe

columns.name: RespondentID
columns.notes: Zero-padded text IDs R01-R52, one per row in order collected

columns.name: Gender
columns.notes: Female / Male / Prefer not to say

columns.name: VisitFrequency
columns.notes: Daily > 2-3 times a week > Once a week > A few times a month > Rarely

columns.name: SatisfactionScore_1to5
columns.notes: 1=very dissatisfied ... 5=very satisfied Likert item; commonly analyzed as numeric/interval by researchers; integer values only

columns.name: AvgWeeklySpend_USD
columns.notes: US dollars, 2 decimals; cell display uses currency number format ($#,##0.00) but underlying stored value is a plain float

clean_table.rule: freq drawn from {Daily,2-3 times a week,Once a week,A few times a month,Rarely} with weights [10,25,30,25,10]; SatisfactionScore = round(clip(N(freq_mean,0.7),1,5)) with freq_mean in {Daily:4.6, 2-3/wk:4.2, 1/wk:3.8, few/month:3.4, Rarely:3.0}; WouldRecommend='Yes' w.p. 0.90 if score>=4, 0.40 if score==3, 0.10 otherwise; AvgWeeklySpend_USD = round(max(2, N(freq_spend_mean,4)),2) with freq_spend_mean in {Daily:32, 2-3/wk:22, 1/wk:14, few/month:9, Rarely:5}; Age ~ Uniform(19,64) integer; Gender weights [Female 46, Male 46, Prefer not to say 8]. Seed=20260920.

intended_analysis: Does satisfaction differ across visit-frequency groups (one-way ANOVA / correlation between frequency rank and satisfaction score)? Does average weekly spend differ by gender or by whether the customer would recommend the cafe (independent t-test)? Is satisfaction score associated with likelihood to recommend (chi-square / logistic)?
mess_applied: Header is on row 3, not row 1 -- a merged title spans row 1 and row 2 is a blank spacer row before the real header
AvgWeeklySpend_USD is displayed with a currency number format in Excel but the underlying cell value is a plain float, not text
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A reader that assumes the header is always row 1 would read the merged title text as column names and treat row 2 (blank) as the first data row, shifting everything down and producing all-null columns.
